before: - Past the standard retirement age: drawing a full old-age pension, or reaching that age, frees the employee from pension and unemployment contributions, but the employer still pays its half ([§ 172(1) SGB VI](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_6/__172.html), [§ 346(3) SGB III](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_3/__346.html)).
after: - **Past the standard retirement age.** Pension and unemployment have different exemption tests. Under [§ 5(4) SGB VI](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_6/__5.html), an ordinarily insured employee drawing a full old-age pension is pension-insurance-free after the end of the month of reaching standard retirement age, unless they waive that exemption; reaching the age alone does not generally end an existing pension-insurance duty. Under [§ 28(1) no. 1 SGB III](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_3/__28.html), unemployment insurance ends at the end of the month of reaching the applicable retirement age. The employer still pays the statutory half contribution for an employee exempt on these grounds ([§ 172(1) SGB VI](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_6/__172.html), [§ 346(3) SGB III](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_3/__346.html)).
